statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 22% because the break of the overnight floor stalled and NQ has lifted about 35 points off a new session low, while a fresh 4.82% 10-year yield and a VIX at its session high keep the environment stressed.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Forecast Tail crosses the block threshold only inside the narrow 12:00-15:00 UTC window covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with a second single-hour checkpoint at the 21:00 UTC Broadcom results. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures stall after a new session low as the 10-year yield prints 4.82%, and the retracement off the low keeps the path two-sided
body: NQ futures traded at 28,979.75 at 10:15 UTC, down 145.75 points or 0.50% from the 29,125.50 previous close, with a second independent quote at 28,963.50 (-0.56%). The structural change from the previous cycle is a stall. An hour ago price was pinned within about twelve points of a 28,957.50 low; since then the session low has extended only marginally to 28,940.50 and price has lifted roughly 35 points back off it. Sixteen points of additional downside in an hour, followed by a retracement, is the opposite of repeated extension after failed pullbacks, and it is why Tail eases to 22% from 23%. The full session range is 28,940.50-29,170.00. Three cross-checks keep the reading in the WATCH band rather than lower. First, the US 10-year yield is 4.82% on Trading Economics live data, above the 4.796% carried in the previous cycle and the highest in this move; the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 31 August shows 4.34% on the 2-year, 4.75% on the 10-year and 5.25% on the 30-year, so the repricing is continuing rather than settling. Second, VIX is 16.82, up 2.94% from a 16.34 close and sitting at the top of a 16.34-16.82 day range - the absolute level is contained but the direction is firmer. Third, the prior session's Finviz cross-asset context, collected at 09:58 UTC and treated as delayed supporting context only, shows semiconductors negative across all seven tracked names with a mean change of -1.06%, and only one of eight megacaps positive; that alignment is real but it is latest-session tone, not live price-path evidence. Two observations argue the other way. S&P 500 E-mini futures are 7,626.00, down only 0.22% in a 7,621.25-7,651.50 range, so the weakness remains concentrated in technology rather than index-wide. And Brent is 94.81, up 0.17% on the day but well off the 97.01 session high inside a 94.55-97.01 range, so the oil channel that has been transmitting the US-Iran escalation into inflation expectations is currently cooling rather than tightening. Stress stays high at 73% because the sovereign-yield repricing, the elevated crude backdrop and an actively priced September policy move are structural conditions that persist regardless of intraday price path. The forward calendar is dense: ADP at 12:15 UTC, the cash open at 13:30 UTC, Factory Orders at 14:00 UTC and EIA crude stocks at 14:30 UTC form a three-hour catalyst cluster, the Fed Beige Book follows at 18:00 UTC, and Broadcom reports after the close at 21:00 UTC - a top-weight constituent whose shares fell 12.6% in a single session after the June quarter despite beating estimates. Confidence is 88% because live quotes for NQ from two independent sources, live VIX, a live 10-year yield, live Brent, a verified seven-day calendar and verified current reporting were all available at the assessment cutoff.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 hours opened with Tail already elevated at 25% during the 1 September European session and peaking at 31% around that day's US cash open, as the US-Iran escalation, the crude surge and the sovereign-yield selloff were priced in. Tail then decayed through the US afternoon and the Asian handover and has held a 20-24% band for the last eighteen published hours, with a single 25% print at 19:00 UTC. Stress stayed persistently high in a 69-77% range throughout. That profile describes a difficult, high-volatility environment in which retracements kept occurring rather than a sustained one-way trend. Three hourly slots have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in a 20-24% band for most of the next 24 hours and lifts it above the block threshold only for the three-hour catalyst cluster from 12:00 to 15:00 UTC, covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with the single highest reading of 28% in the 13:00 UTC hour containing the opening auction. One further hour reaches the threshold at 21:00 UTC around the Broadcom results, where a top-weight semiconductor constituent can move the complex in a thin post-close book. Stress stays high throughout on the crude, sovereign-yield and Fed-repricing backdrop, which is structural rather than intraday, and eases only gradually through the Asian session before ticking up again into the 3 September European morning ahead of ISM Services and Friday's payrolls. Confidence decays with forecast distance because no live price-path evidence exists for later windows at the assessment cutoff.
